name: Junk removal

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)
A.staff: Tasha and Luis (yard hands at the gate)

services.name: Mattress drop-off
services.story: The main story: a $35 mattress drop-off at the yard. Nothing is taken: a YES books it. Alex pays at the gate.

services.name: Mixed load drop-off
services.story: A mixed load, priced at the gate by how much of the bed it fills. Only the $25 minimum is promised, and nothing is owed if Alex says no.

services.name: Remodel debris drop-off
services.story: Remodel debris, priced from Alex's photos at $90. Booked once Sam OKs it; paid at the gate.

services.name: Fridge drop-off
services.story: A $55 fridge drop-off, paid in full when booking, so the refrigerant station is set for it.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer
B.staff: Rafael and Nate (crew leads, each with a helper)

services.name: Junk haul-away
services.story: The main story: a basement and garage, priced on site by how much of the truck it fills: $439. A card is saved for the $89 trip fee, kept only for a late cancel or nobody there. Rosie texts the bill.

services.name: Junk haul-away
services.story: The same cleanout, but nothing is taken up front, the old example owner's way. No fee can be charged for a late cancel.

services.name: Single item pickup
services.story: A $179 single item pickup: an old sofa from the den. A card is saved and charged $179 when Rafael texts DONE.

services.name: Hot tub removal
services.story: A hot tub cut apart and hauled, priced from photos at $640. Sam OKs it. A card is saved for the $89 trip fee; the rest is on the bill.

services.name: Curbside pickup
services.story: A $150 curbside pickup: bags and an old chair left by the curb, paid in full when booking. Nobody needs to be home.

questions_before_times: What's going: a list, and photos (on the secure page)
Where each item is: garage, basement, which floor, and how many flights of stairs
Anything over 300 lb, like a piano, a safe or a hot tub
A fridge or freezer, and is it empty
Any paint, chemicals, propane tanks, asbestos or car batteries (the won't-take list)
At the yard: what's in the load, and the vehicle (a car, a pickup or a trailer)
safety_stop: A gas smell, or a propane tank that's leaking or hissing
Someone hurt, a fire, or a medical emergency
license: Hauling household junk needs a hauler or waste transporter license, permit or registration where the state, county or city asks for one. Many places ask for none: the state's form says which.

messages_never: Door or gate codes, card details, and photos from inside the home: these stay on the secure page.
